- Model tends to overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after sharp spikes; reduce initial forecast peaks by 5–10%.
- After a strong upward spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply a “cool-down” rule: if forecast > true outcome by >10%, reduce next period’s forecast by 5–15%.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits high variance and overconfidence — apply a “mean-reversion bias” correction: average last 5–7 days’ true values as baseline for next forecast.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after a peak, model often fails to recognize it — add a “trend decay” rule: if 3 consecutive true values decline >2%, reduce forecast by 3–8% for next period.
- Model underestimates prices when recent history shows low volatility — apply “volatility floor” rule: if last 5 days’ true values are <70%, forecast floor = 70% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is absent (all 0.00), model should not assume sentiment-driven momentum — treat as “neutral market” and apply “no sentiment amplification” rule: forecast = weighted average of 10–15 day moving average, not trend extrapolation.
